evidence:
Run order: test.sh:213 runs the gates suite (render, constraints) and only after score.py passes, test.sh:224 runs the scored suite with `rewardkit --max-concurrent-agent 1` (serial). The order of dimensions inside a suite is not set in the task. The only statement I found is in another project's README (projects/common-ground-ballot/README.md:34, 'discovers dimensions in alphabetical order and runs one at a time'). On that basis the order would be constraints, render, then functional, polish, visual. The rewardkit source is not installed here (ModuleNotFoundError), and no full configured judge run of this candidate exists. raw-evidence-index.json scope: 'Full configured grading/workload ... absent', and its hashes verified. So the order is unmeasured.

Pristine-seed assumptions exist only in Functional. (1) prompt.md:25 (Z) and judge.toml:335 hro_unread_counts say 'Lena Fischer starts with 1 unread'. Seed: APP-301 has 3 messages and USR-CAN3 read_count 2. (2) prompt.md:25 and judge.toml:407 hro_restart give the seeded Platform Engineer Applied/Screen order and Noor's note 'Strong systems answers; weaker on incident follow-up.' Everything else is relative. prompt.md:15 says 'Earlier reviews may have added jobs, cards and messages. Use your own new jobs and cards ... never rely on starting counts.' T/K allow J3 or the seeded fallback, 'with counts read relative to their values before you act'. hro_thread_latest and hro_thread_earlier grade 'most recent 30' and the remaining count, which do not depend on the 120 total. app_context.md:356-360 says 'never rely on a starting count'.

What earlier dimensions can mutate: render prompt.md:9 says 'Do not create, move or send anything, and do not open any conversation' (read-only). Constraints creates one new job plus one candidate with a unique email (judge.toml:23) and prompt.md:9 says 'Do not move, reject or message anything here'. Neither touches Lena's conversation, the Platform Engineer board order or Noor's note. So under the documented alphabetical order, Functional's absolute Z facts hold for a correct app.

Later dimensions after Functional's heavy mutations:
- Polish prompt.md:14 says 'Use your own new job and cards ... never rely on another review's records' and 'If a message or note box already holds text from an earlier review, record it and clear it before typing your own'. This handles Functional T's leftover Rafael drafts.
- Polish live_thread and earlier_place grade relative to 'its newest message' and the message 'at the top of the view'.
- Polish session_resume's 'both boxes are empty' for Mei is not threatened, because Functional only sends as Mei and leaves no Mei drafts.
- Visual prompt.md:14 is read-only and accepts 'a job with cards in several stages (a seeded job is fine)'. Functional never moves seeded Platform Engineer cards (prompt.md:25 'Move nothing on that job').
- After Functional's restart_app, data persists (test.sh restart helper reuses DB_PATH), so Polish and Visual see a consistent continuing state.

Residual latent exposure if Polish ran before Functional: polish failed_send uses 'a conversation' and session_resume uses 'one conversation', and both send a real message as Rafael. Neither names which one. Recruiters may write in every conversation (hireops_rules.md section 6). If a Polish judge picked Lena's seeded Product Designer conversation (APP-301), Lena's unread would become 2 or more before Functional Z. A correct app would then lose hro_unread_counts (weight 2). Polish line 14's 'the seeded conversations where named' steers judges away from this, but does not forbid it.

Attempted counterexamples:
- Broken app that could pass: an app that hardcodes Lena=1 and the seeded order passes those two legs. Those legs are paired with live relative legs (Tomas count deltas, post-restart comparison of own records), so pristine-seed wording does not create a pass path here. That falls under other rows.
- Conforming app that could fail: only through the unmeasured polish-before-functional order plus a judge choosing APP-301, as described above.

Independence disclosure: one broad workspace grep for ordering wording also printed single matching lines from earlier rounds' SUMMARY.md files (r1/r2/r5). I did not open those files. The verdict rests on the frozen sources cited above.
counterexample: Latent, needs an unmeasured order: if RewardKit ran scored/polish before scored/functional, a Polish judge could carry out hro_pol_failed_send or hro_pol_session_resume as Rafael in Lena Fischer's seeded Product Designer conversation (APP-301). Lena's unread would then be 2 or more, and Functional Z/hro_unread_counts ('Lena Fischer starts with 1 unread') would fail a correct app. Under the alphabetical serial order this README claims (functional first), only the gates run earlier, and they do not touch it.
suggested_fix: Optional hardening, no blocker: have the Polish failed-send and session-resume rows use a conversation of one of the judge's own new cards (or Noor's Platform Engineer conversation), and never Lena Fischer's or Tomas Varga's seeded conversations. Also confirm the scored-suite order in the first full configured verifier log.
